facts.text: Lebanon, Kansas was founded in 1876 by Jackson Allen, who named it after the biblical 'cedars of Lebanon' to honor the creek-side trees that once lined the area.
In 1886 the original settlement moved to its present site, aligning with the Rock Island Railroad, which helped transform Lebanon into a regional shipping hub.
Just 2.6 miles northwest of Lebanon stands a monument marking the geographic center of the contiguous United States, a landmark identified in a 1918 survey.
When Alaska and Hawaii joined the Union, Lebanon’s location became the historical geographic center of the 48 contiguous states.
The documentary 'The Return of the Buffalo: Restoring the Great American Prairie' highlights Lebanon among other Great Plains villages in its exploration of prairie history.
